label: Small Biotech IND Starter — Clinical Benefit/Risk Summary
description: Module 2.5 clinical overview skeleton for an early-phase oncology program.

inputs.drug_class: bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE) antibody targeting CD20 and CD3
inputs.proposed_dosage: 50 mg IV weekly following step-up dosing in Cycle 1 (0.5 mg → 5 mg → 50 mg)
inputs.primary_efficacy: In the Phase 1 dose-escalation study (LT-001, n=24), the overall response rate (ORR) at the recommended Phase 2 dose was 42% (10/24), including 3 complete responses (CR, 12.5%) and 7 partial responses (PR, 29.2%). Responses were observed across all dosing cohorts ≥5 mg.
inputs.secondary_endpoints: Median duration of response: not yet reached (median follow-up 4.2 months). Disease control rate: 62.5% (15/24). Median time to response: 1.4 months (range: 0.9-3.1 months).
inputs.patient_reported_outcomes: EORTC QLQ-C30 assessments showed stable global health status scores through Cycle 4 in responding patients. Fatigue domain scores showed transient worsening in Cycle 1 with recovery by Cycle 2.
inputs.common_adverse_events: CRS: 33% (Grade 1-2: 25%, Grade 3: 8%). Fatigue: 54%. Nausea: 29%. Headache: 21%. Pyrexia: 17%. Neutropenia: 17% (Grade 3: 8%).
inputs.serious_adverse_events: Grade 3 CRS: 2/24 (8%), both managed with tocilizumab and resolved within 48 hours. Grade 3 neutropenia: 2/24 (8%), managed with G-CSF. No Grade 4/5 events. No treatment-related deaths. No dose-limiting toxicities at the recommended Phase 2 dose.
inputs.risk_mitigation: Step-up dosing in Cycle 1 with mandatory 24-hour hospitalization. CRS management per ASTCT consensus grading. Pre-medication with dexamethasone. Dose interruption/reduction guidelines for Grade ≥3 CRS or neurotoxicity. REMS not anticipated based on current safety profile.
inputs.benefit_risk_conclusion: The preliminary efficacy of NovaTide-1 in heavily pretreated R/R DLBCL patients, with an ORR of 42% including durable complete responses, supports a favorable benefit-risk profile. The safety profile is consistent with the BiTE antibody class and manageable with established mitigation strategies. These data support advancement to the Phase 2 expansion cohort.
inputs.unmet_medical_need: Patients with R/R DLBCL after ≥2 prior lines of therapy have limited options and poor prognosis (median OS < 6 months). CAR-T therapy, while effective, is limited by manufacturing time, cost, and specialized center requirements. NovaTide-1 offers an immediately available, off-the-shelf bispecific alternative with manageable outpatient administration after Cycle 1.
